title: Deployment cohort divergence sentinel and rollback choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a cohort-aware sentinel that evaluates quality regressions across staged deployments (canary + A/B cohorts) and coordinates safe automated rollback choreography. This ticket covers the engine that computes cohort divergence signals, the policy layer that translates those signals into actions (halt, throttle, rollback), and the integration points with the rollout controller and Console alerting.

Scope and deliverables:
- Metric ingestion: wire per-cohort eval windows into the metrics pipeline (existing eval jobs + lightweight real-time samplers).
- Divergence detection: implement a multi-metric divergence scorer that supports absolute thresholds and relative drift (percent change), with configurable lookback windows and statistical smoothing.
- Policy engine: policy types (soft-halt, throttle-to-zero, immediate-rollback), severity mapping, and dependency-aware rollback (model changes vs. config flips).
- Simulation harness: replay historical rollout traces and synthetic anomalies to validate false-positive / false-negative behavior.
- Operator UX: Console incident card with root-cause candidate metrics, cohort snapshots, and one-click rollback options.
- Safety: rate-limited automated rollback with cooldown and human-in-the-loop opt-out.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We prioritize low false-positive rollbacks for high-traffic customers; therefore initial policy defaults are conservative (higher thresholds for auto-rollback).
- Use ensemble signals (latency P99, completion rate, hallucination/QA eval scores) instead of single-metric triggers to reduce noise.
- For low-volume cohorts, fall back to longer lookbacks and simulated shadow comparisons to avoid acting on statistical flukes.
- We will avoid embedding heavy ML models in the control plane; detection uses statistical heuristics and simple anomaly detectors.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Divergence scorer runs for each active cohort and emits a normalized "divergence_score" metric.
2) Policy engine evaluates scores every minute and emits a decision event (OK/WARN/FAIL) with an explanation string.
3) Rollout controller accepts decision events and can perform: pause, reduce cohort weight by X%, or full rollback to previous pinned version.
4) Simulation harness demonstrates >=80% precision and >=75% recall on our synthetic anomaly corpus.
5) Console shows cohort-level findings and a rollback action that must include an audit log and PR link when applied.

Instrumentation and observability:
- New metrics: cohort.divergence_score, cohort.policy_decision, cohort.rollback_actions (all tagged with project/model/config).
- Dashboards: per-release cohort heatmap, recent automatic actions, and false-positive tracker for tuning.
- Tracing: include evaluation provenance (eval job id, sample set) in decision events for root cause analysis.

Dependencies and open questions:
- Needs eval-job API extension to return cohort-level summaries (ENG-55670).
- Requires rollout controller hook for dependency-aware rollback (PM asks for integration with release gating API).
- Open: exact default thresholds for P99 latency and QA-score drift (PM to propose baseline after one week of telemetry).

Security & compliance:
- Audit logs for automated actions and human confirmations stored in the Private audit bucket. No customer data flows outside existing telemetry pipelines.

notes_for_release: Controlled rollout in runtime-1.21 behind feature flag 'cohort-divergence-sentinel'. Enable for internal customers first, then staged beta with monitoring and manual opt-out.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: metrics ingestion + divergence scorer (2 weeks). Phase 2: policy engine + simulation harness (2 weeks). Phase 3: rollout-controller integration + Console UX (2 weeks). Staged enablement and one-week telemetry before enabling auto-rollback by default.
retro_criteria: Track auto-rollback precision/recall, number of manual overrides, mean time-to-detect, and customer-reported incidents. Revisit thresholds after 30 days of telemetry.
